Dossier 0.6.7 to 0.7, a reset

Twelve moves toward a leaner Dossier

Six small moves and six large ones, plus one decision first: reshape the current code or rebuild the core from its pieces. The theme is subtraction: fewer controls, fewer blocks, one export, one look. Pick by number.

What Dossier is

Dossier does three things. An agent turns a prompt into a structured document. A person reads it and decides inside it. The agent reads the decisions back and acts. Everything else is weight.

The strongest use is the brainstorm loop: ask for minor and major features, skim, pick by number. 0.7 makes that loop excellent first, then carries plans, reviews, releases, and incidents on the same skeleton.

  1. The static file is for reading and deciding. Editing lives in dossier serve.
  2. One page shape, many kinds.
  3. Every control is explainable in one sentence.
  4. Budgets are tests, and the numbers go down.

Where it fractured

Every idea from the June brainstorm shipped. Together they produced a reader shell that carries authoring tools, six overlapping exports, and a runtime every artifact pays for. Measured on the showcase example:

7 controlsIn the top bar. Four of them edit the document rather than read it.
11 exportsIn the Export menu, plus 14 buttons in the Export Center, for two ideas.
5 modalsShipped in every file, including read-only briefs.
74 KBRuntime JavaScript in every artifact, mostly state packets and the block editor.
67 KBCSS for all 43 blocks, skins, and theme packs, whether or not they appear.
43 blocksFifteen are overlapping process variants.
28 toolsOn the MCP server over ten packet schemas. The brainstorm asked for four.
2 renderersA string renderer and a React port kept in step by hand.

Rebuild or reshape

Together, the twelve moves are a rebuild. The question is whether to do it inside the current tree one subtraction at a time, or to stand up a new core beside it and cut over when the examples build. Same destination; the difference is how long the code sits half-broken and what survives by accident.

A clean core rests on five concepts:

  1. Kind. A preset: sections, facets, how the reader replies.
  2. Section. Content parts, no state.
  3. Item. A numbered thing in a board with size, effort, impact, dependencies, and facets.
  4. Facet. A labeled paragraph on an item, in fixed order.
  5. Decision. What the reader said: picked, a verdict, a note. The only state.

A release checklist is a board of gates. An incident review is a board of findings with a timeline in front. A patch review is a board of files whose facet is a diff. The concepts stay put; the kinds grow, and a kind is forty lines.

modelOne schema for kind, meta, sections, items, facets, decisions. Old block names accepted as aliases.
kindsSix presets shipped, custom kinds from a pack. Small readable files, not code.
rendererOne string renderer, zero runtime dependencies. React becomes a typed wrapper around its output.
readerContents, search, theme, collapse, copy, decisions, pick. Under 20 KB.
studioEverything that edits, injected by serve, never in the file.
agentThe skill plus four MCP tools: create, render, read decisions, apply decisions.
build-timeKept: highlighting, diagrams, math, diff parser, DOCX and PDF, CLI, tests, examples as fixtures.

In practice: new core beside the old, port content blocks against the examples, then boards and decisions, then the reader, then serve. Cut over when every example builds through the new core. Either path is days of agent time; the rebuild spends fewer of them half-broken.

The merged format

The June brainstorm gave each idea a how-it-works, an experience, a why, and an unlocks line. The front door page gave each feature fixed facets, size and effort chips, an impact meter, a summary table, and a closing pick. Merged, they are the brainstorm kind, and the facet vocabulary generalizes.

The new shell

The contents column sits left and sticky. Items are separated by hairlines, not boxes. Four things on a page are objects: the stat strip, spec lists, tables, and the also-considered rows. The one saturated block is the closing pick.

≥ 1100pxTwo columns: 208px contents rail, content column, 1360px frame.
820 to 1099pxOne column. Contents become a wrapping row of chips.
≤ 719pxFacet labels stack above their text. Tables scroll in their own box.
printContents and controls hidden, every item expanded, hairlines kept.

1 Shell reset

The top bar drops to four things: where you are, search, theme, one export.

How it works

Edit, Blocks, Evidence, Theme Studio, the progress bar, back-to-top, and the Export Center leave the static build and live only under dossier serve. The palette lists only what the page has.

Reader

Opens a document, not a workbench. Every control does something a reader wants.

Agent

Authoring is unchanged. The skill describes one action: copy for agent.

Unlocks

Item 8 becomes a refactor of code already outside the artifact.

Risk

Editing inside a shared file stops working until it is opened in serve. Say so in the README.

2 Left table of contents

A sticky left column with grouped, numbered entries; a chip row on narrow screens.

How it works

Kinds declare which sections are frame, which are items, and which are the rest. Numbers come from board order. Below 1100px the list becomes chips.

Reader

Sees the shape of the document before reading it and jumps by number.

Agent

Never assigns numbers by hand.

Unlocks

The new shell, and a wider measure without a cramped column.

3 Type and token swap

The front door tokens become Dossier's, with the accent moved to crimson and dark tuned separately.

How it works

Thirteen color roles plus three font stacks. Three-state theming. Web fonts are opt-in with meta.fonts: "google"; the system stack carries the look without them.

Reader

Light is the base, dark is retuned, and the toggle wins over the system setting.

Agent

Sets one field, meta.theme.accent, and nothing else.

Unlocks

Item 11. With tokens this small, skins have nothing left to override.

Risk

Crimson sits close to a coral risk label, so risk moves to ochre. Blue remains the alternative accent.

minor Effort S impact 4/5

4 Facets block

A labeled-paragraph list in fixed order, plus size, effort, and impact rendered as chips and meters.

How it works

Items carry size, effort, impact, and a facets array. The renderer draws the meta row, the numbered title, the one-line summary, and the facets. Risk and Note take the colored label.

Reader

Every item has the same facets in the same order, so items compare by scanning one label column.

Agent

Gets the vocabulary per kind and the rule that order never changes.

Unlocks

Items 5 and 7 derive from these fields.

minor Effort S impact 4/5

5 Summary table from the board

The board emits its own table above the items: number, title, size, effort, impact, depends on.

How it works

summary: true renders the table with a generated legend. Depends-on values are validated, so a dangling reference fails the build.

Reader

Skims one table, then jumps. The biggest reading improvement for long plans.

Agent

Never writes the table, so it cannot drift from the items.

Unlocks

Item 6, and the stat strip that counts sizes automatically.

Depends on

6 Pick by number

The closing action copies the selection as one line an agent can act on, with JSON behind it.

How it works

Ticks and notes anywhere on the page fill the closing block. Copy gives 1, 3, 4, 7. Notes: 3: keep blue. or the same as JSON. This replaces the decisions, handoff, and prompt exports.

Reader

Reads, ticks, copies one line, pastes it into the thread.

Agent

Parses the line or reads the JSON through MCP. Both say the same thing.

8 Two-tier runtime

The static file carries a reader runtime under 20 KB; everything that edits moves to serve.

How it works

A core (contents, search, theme, collapse, copy, pick) plus per-block modules included only when the block appears. Editing, evidence, imports, Theme Studio, and CodeMirror become the studio bundle serve injects. Budgets are tests.

Reader

Files open instantly and behave the same everywhere.

Agent

Authoring is unchanged; editing round-trips target serve.

Unlocks

A React wrapper that only matches the reader, and a rule that plugins ship no runtime.

Risk

The largest change. Do it after item 1 has hidden the surfaces, so the split is mechanical.

Depends on

9 Block consolidation

Forty-three blocks become about twenty-two by folding overlapping families, with old names kept as aliases.

How it works

board absorbs four board kinds, evidence four evidence kinds, diff two, gates two, log four. Validation maps old names with a deprecation warning; 0.8 removes the aliases.

Reader

Fewer idioms to learn. A board looks like a board whatever it holds.

Agent

Chooses from a catalog that fits on one screen.

Unlocks

A third of the CSS and render code goes away.

Risk

MCP tools and packet schemas name the old blocks. Do item 10 first.

Depends on

10 One export contract

Seven export shapes become two files: the decided model and a decisions document.

How it works

slug.dossier.json is the model with decisions applied. slug.decisions.md is the reply, notes, and verdicts as Markdown with JSON inside. Source, state, merged, handoff, prompt, and digest go away as names.

Reader

There is the document and there is what they decided.

Agent

Reads one Markdown document to learn the decisions and one JSON file to rebuild.

Unlocks

Items 8 and 9, and a CLI with far fewer flags.

Risk

Workspaces and release evidence consume the old packets. Give them the decisions document plus a compatibility reader.

Skins, theme packs, and the in-artifact Theme Studio retire in favor of one look with one accent override.

The skin layer and theme packs are removed. meta.theme.accent and meta.fonts are the only presentation fields. Theme Studio survives only in serve, as an accent preview.

Reader

Every Dossier looks like the same product.

Agent

Nothing to choose, nothing to get wrong.

Unlocks
